rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.3, two-year (2018-2020) randomized block field experiment in Yuanyang County with FI, DI and RF under three cropping systems, measuring SWC, SNC, LAI, DM and yield, plus WHCNS model runs calibrated on year 1 and validated on year 2. Q2: Section 3.2 and Table 7, DI cropping systems 2H1Y, 3H2Y and 1H1Y received 34%, 36% and 40% less irrigation than FI (water-metered applications) while yields were maintained or higher; seasonal water saving 31% for wheat and 40% for maize; all cropping systems had highest WUE under DI (Table 6). Q4: Table 7 and Section 3.3, DI lowered simulated soil evaporation (8-74%), drainage (61-74%) and runoff (37-49%) and measured SWC was kept at optimum level (Section 4.1); these are intermediate pathways for water saving. Q8: Section 4.4, authors state drainage, ET, runoff were not measured so simulated water consumption carries large uncertainty, and more observed datasets would be needed for calibration. Q9: Table 6 reports WUE values with <U+00B1> standard errors for each crop and annual average under DI, FI and RF.
rows.notes: The review passage attributes 34% to winter wheat and 36-40% to maize; the study actually gives 34%, 36% and 40% as reductions for the 2H1Y, 3H2Y and 1H1Y cropping systems (two-year totals), and seasonal savings of 31% (wheat) and 40% (maize). The irrigation savings are differences in applied amounts rather than measured consumption; ET, drainage and runoff are model outputs validated only indirectly through soil water content. The <U+00B1> values apply to WUE, not to the percentage irrigation saving itself. Single site, one soil, plot scale.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.2-2.3, two-year field experiment with measured grain yields at physiological maturity. Q2: Section 3.2 and Table 6, DI 2H1Y, 3H2Y and 1H1Y produced two-year totals of 39829, 29619 and 21777 kg/ha versus 36962, 29542 and 21290 under FI; annual average yield order DI > FI > RF with significance letters; Fig. 4 shows measured and simulated yields. Q4: Section 2.3 and 4.1, measured soil water content, LAI and dry matter; authors report FI induced excessive SWC whereas DI maintained SWC at an optimum level, promoting growth. Q8: Section 4.4, limited observed datasets for calibration and large uncertainties in simulated yields; Section 3.2 notes no significant DI-FI yield difference within the same cropping system for some crops. Q9: Table 6 gives grain yield means <U+00B1> standard errors per crop and annual average.
rows.notes: Yield gains from DI over FI are modest (about 1-8%); the text is internally inconsistent, stating in one place no significant difference between DI and FI within a cropping system and elsewhere a significant difference. Simulated yields are compared with measured ones but the model was calibrated on the same experiment, so this is not independent triangulation. Single site, plot scale, two years.

rows.evidence: Q1: Field experiment plus WHCNS simulations as above. Q2: Section 3.4 and Table 8, simulated annual N leaching under DI was 58%, 62% and 59% lower than under FI for 2H1Y, 3H2Y and 1H1Y, with NH3 volatilization reduced 33-55%; Table 6 shows NUE significantly higher under DI (e.g. 32.12 vs 26.46 kg/kg for 2H1Y); the model was validated against measured soil mineral N profiles to 100 cm (Table 3, Fig. 3, nRMSE mostly 10-28%). Q4: Table 7 and Table 3, drainage (the leaching carrier) simulated to fall 61-74% under DI and soil mineral N concentration measured by depth. Q8: Section 4.4, authors explicitly state N leaching, volatilization and denitrification were not measured so simulated N fates carry large uncertainties. Q9: Table 6 reports NUE with <U+00B1> standard errors.
rows.notes: N leaching reductions are model outputs only; the model was validated against soil water and soil mineral N content from the same site but N leaching itself was never measured, so Q2 is a borderline yes. Table 8 N fate values carry no dispersion; the <U+00B1> values apply to NUE. The passage's framing (N leaching reduced 'by improving NUE') is the review's inference; the study reports both but does not test that causal chain. 'Soil health' is a loose label for N leaching reduction. Single site, plot scale.

notes: Full text available including methods, results, discussion, limitations and references. Study is a single-site, two-year, plot-scale field experiment coupled with the WHCNS model; yields, soil water and soil mineral N were measured, whereas ET, drainage, runoff and N fates are simulated outputs not directly validated.
